method: Read-only Vivado open_checkpoint and all_fanin to actual quantizer loaded register asynchronous CLR pins
recovery_state_encoding: Two FDCE state bits, sequential binary 00=NORMAL,01=RESET_CORE,10=READ_TABLE,11=WRITE_TABLE; not one-hot recoded
hazard: At WRITE_TABLE 11 to NORMAL 00, if recovery bit1 falls before bit0, the decode temporarily sees01 and asserts asynchronous CLR after all128 entries were replayed
logical_effect: A CLR pulse can erase quantizer loaded flags while channel returns NORMAL; tables_ready stays false with busy false and no replay trigger
recommended_fix: Use a dedicated registered core_reset bit. Assert it on abort_now and deassert it in the RESET_CORE branch; core_rst_n=rst_n&&!core_reset. Never derive an asynchronous reset from multibit state decoding.
notes: This is a demonstrated structural reset hazard consistent with the raw hardware failure syndrome, not an oscilloscope/ILA pulse measurement. The original zero-delay FSM/table replay logic can still pass ordinary RTL simulation.
